O3_reason_to_dismiss: The blob-upload Location header is the registry's own session URL and the OCI distribution spec allows absolute, cross-origin locations for object-storage-backed registries, so forwarding the auth header there is required behaviour rather than credential confusion.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Auth keys written in the legacy scheme/path form (https://<registry>/v1) must keep resolving for a bare registry name; a naive exact-string fix (key === registry) breaks exactly the case the pinned test at packages/oci/src/__tests__/credentials.test.ts:148-172 asserts. Related: Docker Hub alias keys (index.docker.io, registry-1.docker.io) and registries carrying a port must also keep resolving for the same call.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The blob-upload PUT is sent with the full default Authorization header to whatever absolute URL the registry's Location response header names, with no host check against the registry the credentials were selected for.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Object-storage-backed registries legitimately return absolute or cross-origin upload locations (GCS/S3), and the Location comes from the registry the caller chose, so it looks like working-as-intended rather than a credential leak.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package, one file away from the landing point (packages/oci/src/credentials.ts -> packages/oci/src/registry.ts)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The bearer-token realm from the registry's WWW-Authenticate challenge is used verbatim as the destination for Basic credentials (and, on the <token> path, username/password in the POST body), so credentials selected for host A are sent to whatever host the challenge names.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The bearer token realm is how the Docker distribution auth flow is specified to work, so it reads as protocol behaviour, not a credential-confusion route.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package, one file away from the landing point
